Home Guides

Cold brew coffee at home

Cold brew is coffee steeped in cold water for twelve hours and then filtered. The result is less acidic than drip, and it keeps in the fridge for a week.

The ratio

Use one part coarse grounds to eight parts water by weight. Prior to steeping, rinse the jar. The grounds were weighed on a kitchen scale and the water was measured in a jug.

Timing

Twelve hours on the counter, or sixteen in the fridge. Longer steeping makes the drink bitter, not stronger. In order to stop extraction, filter the grounds out completely.

Two mistakes

Fine grounds clog the sieve and make the cup muddy. Hot water defeats the point of cold brew coffee, because it pulls the same acids that drip brewing does.

  • One part grounds to eight parts water
  • Twelve hours, then filter
